# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XXXIV. IDA VISITS THE HILL

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Ida moved to the upper floor. Rupert and Grace were currently walking toward Fern Hollow under the nascent moon, since the fairy-like music of Tobias’s jews-harp had reached them from that direction, leading them to suspect the Carrows' presence and the start of amusement. Ida lacked the desire to join them. Heading to her private chamber initially, she seated herself upon the bed to weep briefly. Having someone replace her beloved mother was against her wishes. She detested the thought of a stepmother who would despise her and cause her father to despise her as well. Nevertheless, her father suffered such profound sorrow—and she was obligated to perform whatever action might increase his happiness. Only a single course of action was open to her—and from the instant she departed the study, she recognized her obligation to execute it. Yet it presented an extremely difficult task.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0000 }

Once Ida had finished weeping copiously, she dried her tears and proceeded to the spare room. Because the blind had been left down and the window kept closed for an extended period, the room was pitch-black and somewhat stale. Fresh air was not something Aunt Martha cared for. However, since no one ever considered closing a door inside the manse, this was less of an issue, except on occasions when an unlucky minister stayed overnight and had no choice but to inhale the air of the spare room.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0001 }

Inside the spare room sat a closet, and hanging deep within its depths was a gray silk dress. After stepping inside the closet and closing the door, Ida dropped to her knees and buried her face in the soft folds of silk. Her mother had worn it as a wedding-dress. A faint, sweet, and haunting scent, resembling a love that lingers, still filled it. Being in that spot always made Ida feel extremely near to her mother—just like she was kneeling at her feet with her head resting on her lap. Whenever life became excessively difficult, she would go there once in a great while.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0002 }

“Mother,” she murmured toward the dress of gray silk, “you will never be forgotten by me, mother, and my love for you will forever be the greatest. Yet this must be done by me, mother, since father suffers such great unhappiness. It is certain to me that his unhappiness would not be desired by you. Also, my behavior toward her will be exceptionally good, mother, as I endeavor to love her, notwithstanding her potential resemblance to what stepmothers always were according to Mary Stubbs.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0003 }

Some splendid, soul-deep power was borne away from her hidden altar by Ida. On that night, with the marks of tears yet shining upon her dear, grave, small face, she drifted off to sleep in peace.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0004 }

During the following afternoon, she dressed in her finest hat and gown. They were quite worn out. With the exception of Grace and Ida, all the other young girls in the Glen possessed new garments that summer. Mary Stubbs possessed a beautiful gown made of white embroidered lawn, accompanied by shoulder bows and a sash of scarlet silk. However, Ida was unbothered by her worn appearance on this day. Being extremely tidy was her sole desire. Her face was washed with care. Her black hair was brushed by her until it reached a satiny smoothness. After mending a pair of runs in her single set of decent stockings, she neatly fastened her shoelaces. Polishing her shoes was something she wished to do, yet finding any blacking proved impossible for her. At last, she quietly left the manse, traveling down through Fern Hollow, ascending through the whispering woods, and emerging onto the road passing by the house on the hill. Because the journey was rather lengthy, Ida felt fatigued and heated upon her arrival.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0005 }

Her eyes caught Clementine Ainslie positioned beneath a tree within the garden, prompting her to creep by the dahlia beds toward her. A book rested upon Clementine’s lap, yet her eyes were fixed on the far distance over the harbour, accompanied by rather mournful thoughts. Lately, living in the house on the hill had lacked pleasantness. Harriet had refrained from sulking—Harriet had acted like a brick. Nevertheless, unuttered feelings remain palpable, making the silence that fell between the two women intolerably expressive on occasion. Every single familiar element that used to render life sweet had acquired a bitter taste currently. Furthermore, Lionel Fairlie carried out recurring intrusions, alternating between bullying and coaxing Harriet. Clementine held the belief that this situation would conclude with his hauling Harriet away alongside him eventually, an outcome Clementine felt she would welcome almost gladly. While life would become dreadfully solitary at that point, it would cease to be filled with dynamite.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0006 }

A gentle, hesitant pat upon her shoulder awakened her from her disagreeable musings. Looking back, Ida Ashdown met her gaze.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0007 }

“My goodness, dear Ida, was it on foot that you made the journey up here through such intense heat?”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0008 }

“Indeed,” Ida remarked, “I arrived in order to—I arrived in order to—”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0009 }

Yet accomplishing the task she had arrived for proved exceedingly difficult for her to voice. Her speech deserted her, and tears welled up in her eyes.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0010 }

“What is wrong, Ida, my little girl? You should not fear sharing it with me.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0011 }

Clementine placed her arm about the slender small figure and pulled the youngster near herself. Her eyes possessed great beauty—her contact was so gentle that Ida gathered bravery.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0012 }

“I arrived—to request that you—wed father,” she panted.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0013 }

For a brief instant, Clementine said nothing because she was completely astonished. Her gaze rested uncomprehendingly on Ida.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0014 }

“Oh, please do not be mad, sweet Miss Ainslie,” Ida begged. “You know, it is being said by everyone that your refusal to marry father is due to our being so terrible. He feels very miserable concerning it. Therefore, I decided to come and inform you that our misbehavior is never intentional. And provided you just marry father, every one of us will attempt to be well-behaved and execute exactly what you command. I am certain that we will not cause you any difficulty. Please, Miss Ainslie.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0015 }

Clementine’s thoughts had been racing. It was clear to her that idle speculation had planted this false notion in Ida’s head. With the girl, she needed to be completely candid and genuine.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0016 }

“Ida, dear,” she murmured gently. “My inability to become the wife of your father is not on account of you poor little souls. Such an idea never entered my mind. You are not bad—I never imagined you were. There—Ida, there was a completely different reason.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0017 }

“Do you not like father?” Ida inquired, raising eyes filled with reproach. “Oh, Miss Ainslie, you have no idea how nice he is. I am certain he would be a good husband to you.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0018 }

Despite her confusion and suffering, Clementine was unable to suppress a faint, wry smile.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0019 }

“Oh, do not poke fun, Miss Ainslie,” Ida exclaimed with intense feeling. “Father is deeply upset over the matter.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0020 }

“I believe you are in error, my love,” Clementine remarked.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0021 }

“I am not. I am certain I am not. Oh, Miss Ainslie, Rupert had been bad, so father was intending to whip him yesterday—and father was unable to accomplish it since, as you know, he lacked practice in whipping. Thus, once Rupert emerged and informed us that father felt extremely upset, I crept into the study to discover whether I might assist him—he prefers me to soothe him, Miss Ainslie—and he failed to hear me enter, allowing me to overhear his words. I will inform you, Miss Ainslie, provided you permit me to whisper it into your ear.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0022 }

Ida spoke in a urgent whisper. A deep blush covered Clementine’s face. Therefore, John Ashdown continued to hold her in his heart. His feelings remained unaltered. Furthermore, his devotion had to be remarkably deep for him to have uttered those words—deeper than she had ever imagined it to be. For a brief pause, she remained seated without moving, running her fingers through Ida’s hair. After that, she remarked,
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0023 }

“Ida, would you carry a short note to your father for me?”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0024 }

“Oh, will you be marrying him, Miss Ainslie?” Ida inquired with enthusiasm.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0025 }

“Maybe—if he genuinely desires me to do so,” Clementine answered, turning red once more.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0026 }

“I’m happy—I’m happy,” Ida uttered courageously. Afterwards, her lips trembling, she gazed upward. “Oh, Miss Ainslie, you will not cause father to oppose us—you will not cause him to despise us, will you?” she asked imploringly.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0027 }

Clementine gave another gaze.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0028 }

“Ida Ashdown! Is it your belief that I would commit such an act? What on earth made you think of that?”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0029 }

“According to Mary Stubbs, every stepmother behaved in that manner—hating their stepchildren and driving their fathers to hate them as well—because simply being a stepmother compelled them to act that way”—
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0030 }

“My poor child! Even so, you traveled up here and requested that I wed your father since you desired his happiness? You are a sweetheart—a heroine—or a brick, to use Harriet's phrase. Listen to what I am telling you, dearest, with great care. Mary Stubbs is an unwise young girl lacking extensive knowledge, and regarding certain matters, she is terribly incorrect. Turning your father against you is something I would not ever contemplate. Every one of you would be dearly loved by me. Taking the place of your own mother is not my desire—in your hearts, that must forever belong to her. However, becoming a stepmother is also not my plan. My wish is to serve as your friend, helper, and pal. Wouldn't that be pleasant, Ida—were you, Grace, Rupert, and Tobias able to simply view me as a fine, cheerful pal—a tall elder sister?”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0031 }

“Oh, it would be lovely,” Ida shouted, her face completely altered. Impulsively, her arms wrapped around Clementine’s neck. Her happiness was so immense that she felt capable of taking flight on wings.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0032 }

“Are the rest of them—are Grace and the boys of one mind with you regarding stepmothers?”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0033 }

“No. Mary Stubbs was never believed by Grace. It was dreadfully foolish of me to believe her as well. You are loved by Grace already—ever since poor Adam was eaten, she has loved you. And it will be thought jolly by Tobias and Rupert. Oh, Miss Ainslie, when you come to live with us, will you—could you—teach me to cook—a little—and sew—and—and—and do things? Nothing is known by me. Much trouble I won't be—fast is how I'll try to learn.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0034 }

“My dear, I will instruct you and render whatever assistance I am able to. Now, you will not utter a single thing to anyone regarding this, will you—not even to Grace, until your father himself informs you that you are permitted? And you will remain to take tea with me?”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0035 }

“Oh, I appreciate it—however—however—I believe I should return immediately to give father the letter,” stammered Ida. “You understand, it will make him happy that much earlier, Miss Ainslie.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0036 }

“I understand,” Clementine remarked. Proceeding to the dwelling, she composed a message and handed it to Ida. As soon as that little maiden had scampered away, a quivering package of delight, Clementine moved toward Harriet, who happened to be podding peas upon the rear veranda.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0037 }

“Harriet,” she stated, “Ida Ashdown was recently at this place requesting that I become her father's wife.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0038 }

Harriet raised her eyes, studying what was written across her sister’s features.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0039 }

“And what do you intend to do?” she asked.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0040 }

“It’s highly probable.”
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0041 }

Harriet continued to shell peas for a short time. After that, she abruptly raised her hands to her face. Her dark-browed eyes were filled with tears.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0042 }

“I—I hope happiness lies ahead for everyone,” she uttered, half laughing and half sobbing.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0043 }

Farther down at the vicarage, Ida Ashdown, glowing, flushed, and victorious, stepped courageously into the study of her father and placed a letter on his desk. The pale skin of his face reddened when his eyes caught the neat, delicate penmanship that was so familiar to him. Unsealing the letter, he found it to be brief—yet reading its contents stripped two decades from his age. In it, Clementine requested that he meet her by the spring in Fern Hollow at dusk that very night.
{: #nw-v05-c34-p0044 }
